chapter: Hippolyte Charles and the country clubs
title: Hippolyte Charles again: country club band and pay
summary: Charles was a first-class trumpeter; Dawson repeats the country-club band lineup and two-dollar-an-hour pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: well i think of it we keep jumping around changing the subject the other night you mentioned hippolyte charles and yeah what kind of a trumpet carnet player he was he was a first class trumpet player

he was a first class trumpet player where did you work with him what i worked with him at the new Orleans country club i worked at the lions club he had in other words he had a contract with the the lions club the autocrat club and the New Orleans country club and that time we was getting all them two dollars an hour like the musicians getting one

we was getting it then, when things was good, when things was cheap. We used to play a tea dance at the New Orleans Country Club on Sunday evening for two hours, and we used to play every Saturday night out there for a regular dance for the club. And then we'd get our check at the end of the week. See, they paid off with a check. Now he had Camilla Tile on the piano. He had, what do you call this, a trombone player with, got his leg cut off. Big Gasp. No, no, not Big Gasp. Sonny Henry? Sonny Henry. He had Sonny Henry on the trombone. He had Big R on the violin. And I was playing penna banjo. And let's see now, we had, he had Joe Welch on the drum. And he had trombone. And he had Lorenzo Tile, I think it was, on the saxophone. He had about seven, eight pieces out there. And he had Albert Glenny on the bass. And that's right, that was his band. Those early bands we were talking about,
